title: Elastic token-lease throttling for hot-KV high-QPS workloads
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: During sustained high QPS with skewed key distributions we observe cascading microbatch backpressure, high KV cache churn, and episodic GPU OOMs. Current threshold policies use static per-microbatch token limits which either allow long-tail spikes to exhaust GPU headroom or over-throttle requests and increase end-to-end latency for healthy tenants.

Goal: Implement an admission controller that uses elastic, probabilistic token leasing plus KV coldening signals and quantized GPU headroom buckets to provide: (1) bounded tail latency under hot-key surges, (2) graceful degradation instead of OOMs, and (3) preservation of KV hit-rate for steady clients. This should integrate with the continuous batching runtime and the existing KV cache eviction path.

High-level approach:
- Token leasing: allocate short-duration token leases to incoming microbatches (lease granularity = tokens), with a probabilistic refresh path for hot requests. Leases decay over time; tenants accumulate a small amount of reclaimable credit when they underuse their allocation.
- Elastic thresholds: token limits per microbatch are not fixed; they scale with a per-GPU quantized headroom bucket (e.g., 5% buckets of available GPU memory and slab occupancy). When headroom is low, new leases are reduced automatically; when headroom rises, leases increase.
- KV coldening: use a KV 'coldness' signal (recent-access histogram + last-access TTL) to preemptively compact and evict cold shards during sustained pressure rather than reactive bulk eviction. Coldening reduces spike eviction cost and preserves hot-key entries.
- Probabilistic preemption and soft-fallbacks: when immediate headroom is unavailable, certain leases are probabilistically deferred (short backoff) or routed to a CPU/quantized fallback variant. This creates a graded degradation instead of sudden failures.
- Telemetry & feedback loop: run-time metrics (lease grant rate, avg lease length, KV hit-rate, GPU slab occupancy, p50/p95/p99 token wait time) feed a control loop that tunes probabilistic parameters and headroom-to-lease mapping.

Design details:
1) Admission controller components:
   - LeaseIssuer service co-located with batching scheduler. On enqueue, microbatch requests a lease size and duration. The Issuer consults GPUHeadroomMap and TenantCredits ledger.
   - GPUHeadroomMap: lightweight per-GPU quantized buckets (0-100% by 5% steps) computed from slab allocator and CUDA memory metrics.
   - TenantCredits: a per-tenant decaying credit counter that accumulates on underuse to avoid penalizing bursty but fair tenants.
   - KVColdScore: per-shard coldness score derived from access histograms and compaction history. ColdScore biases eviction candidates.

2) Lease algorithm (high-level):
   - baseline_lease = min(requested_tokens, headroom_bucket_factor * requested_tokens)
   - if TenantCredits > threshold => grant bonus up to credit_cap
   - if KVColdScore indicates high eviction pressure => reduce lease by cold_penalty
   - apply probabilistic defer with p = f(headroom_utilization, tenant_priority) to spread spikes

3) Eviction & coldening path:
   - when GPU slab pressure is high, trigger KVColdCompaction rather than immediate full eviction. Compact small or fragmented cold entries and perform batched evictions from cold-ranked shards.

4) Fallback routing:
   - If grant == 0 or deferred, router can: (a) queue with exponential jitter (b) downgrade to quantized model variant (lower mem) (c) route to dedicated burst capacity if available.

Safety and checks:
- Hard global safety cap prevents aggregate lease grants beyond a safe GPU memory watermark to prevent OOMs.
- Lease bookkeeping persisted in-memory with periodic checkpoint to allow deterministic rollback on crashes.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- Key metrics: lease_grant_rate, avg_lease_size, p50/p95/p99 wait_time_for_lease, kv_hit_rate, gpu_slab_util_pct, eviction_ops_per_sec, fallback_routing_pct.
- Target: under a 10k QPS sustained hot-key workload (80/20 skew), p99 latency for generation <= 200ms (current baseline ~320ms) and no GPU OOMs in canary runs. KV hit-rate should not drop more than 5% from baseline in steady-state loads.

Operational considerations and knobs:
- Configs: headroom_bucket_width, tenant_credit_decay_sec, coldness_ttl, probabilistic_defer_curve, fallback_priority_order. These are runtime flags surfaced in Console for tuning and experimentation.

Security/Privacy: uses internal runtime metrics only; no customer PII required.

Why this is different from previous efforts: existing tickets focus on hard microbatch ceilings and static eviction heuristics. This design blends tenancy-aware credits, probabilistic admission, and preemptive KV coldening to avoid bulk churn and provide smoother tail behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Control loop implements quantized GPU headroom buckets and maps them to dynamic lease multipliers
LeaseIssuer grants and records leases with duration; metrics emitted for grant_rate, avg_lease_size, and wait_time
KV coldening compaction path reduces reactive bulk eviction during sustained pressure in benchmark tests
Canary (5% traffic) under a synthetic 10k QPS hot-key test preserves p99 latency <= 200ms and causes no GPU OOMs
Fallback routing triggers for deferred leases and is observable in Console with toggleable priority order
Config knobs exposed in Console and documented in the design doc for live tuning
tasks: Write RFC describing LeaseIssuer, headroom buckets, TenantCredits, and KVColdScore
Implement GPUHeadroomMap and expose slab metrics to runtime (C++/Rust runtime change)
Add TenantCredits ledger and decay logic in admission controller
Implement probabilistic defer and fallback routing in scheduler
Implement KV coldening compaction path and test harness for eviction pressure
Add telemetry (lease grants, wait times, cold scores) and Console dashboards
Run canary and synthetic stress tests, iterate on parameters
Rollout plan: canary (5%) -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with kill-switch and runtime feature flag
notes: 2025-10-16: Initial spike analysis shows OOMs correlated with eviction storms when hot-key eviction touched >40% of slab entries
2025-10-22: Decided to use quantized buckets (5% increments) to keep decision logic CPU-light and cache-friendly
2025-10-29: Trade-off: TenantCredits increases complexity but reduces false positives for bursty tenant patterns; accepted after small prototype
2025-11-02: Integration note: fallback routing will reuse existing dedicated capacity routing codepath to avoid duplicated sync logic
2025-11-04: Miguel implemented a local prototype of probabilistic defer; observed 15% reduction in eviction spikes in bench runs
